name: Sock Stage
one_liner: Put your phone inside a sock puppet behind the sofa; the TV becomes the puppet theatre, and a giant puppet speaks with your voice.
impossible_on_phone: The phone is inside the sock on the puppeteer's hidden hand, so its screen cannot be seen by anyone; the show only exists on a stage the audience faces across the room.
ten_second_shot: A sock rises over the sofa back; on the TV a dragon rises with it. 'Hellooo!' and the dragon's jaw flaps in time with the voice. The hand shakes, the dragon headbutts the frame and stars fly. A second sock appears and a frog pops up on the other side of the stage.
interaction: TV: the stage (curtain, backdrop, up to four puppets, a 'director' card with the scene). Phone: inside the sock; tilt/turn = head, raise/lower = puppet enters/exits, shake = bump/jump, mic loudness = mouth; its screen is never looked at. Remote: OK opens the curtain / next scene (keeps Vega awake), Up/Down picks the backdrop, Back returns to the booth.
mechanism: Phone browser: DeviceOrientationEvent (beta/gamma -> head pitch and turn; raised vs lowered from beta sign), DeviceMotionEvent jerk -> bump, the existing mic RMS `level` message at ~20 Hz -> jaw opening, Screen Wake Lock so sensors keep running. ~30 Hz compact messages over couch-link (host + N players; presence assigns puppet slots). TV: Image parts (head, jaw, body) moved with RN Animated transforms on plain Views, no SVG and no TV audio (the voices are live in the room, which sidesteps the simulator's audio problems). Optional: the coach-agent shape (Strands on Bedrock AgentCore) becomes the 'director' that proposes a one-line scene for the current cast, with a fallback list.
demo_honesty: One adult, one sock, one phone: show pairing, slide the hand up behind the sofa, talk, nod, shake. A second puppet appears only if a friend holds a second phone; otherwise the video says 'up to four' and shows one. Claim 'the mouth follows how loud you are', never lip-sync. Only the loudness number leaves the phone, not audio, same invariant as Strumble.
biggest_risk: iOS Safari needs a tap-granted DeviceOrientation permission and its yaw drifts; the mic inside a thick sock can read low. Mitigate with a thin sock, the mic at the sock opening, a per-puppet auto-gain on the RMS, and a tap-to-recentre.

name: Lantern
one_liner: The TV is a pitch-dark cave and your phone is the torch; things in the dark only move when your beam isn't on them.
impossible_on_phone: A torch has to be pointed away from you at something across the room; the beam and the creatures live on a big surface the whole room watches, while the phone's own screen stays black.
ten_second_shot: Black screen. A torch beam sweeps across stone walls and lands on a creature frozen mid-step. The beam slides away to a glinting key; when it swings back the creature is a metre closer, still frozen. The kids on the sofa scream 'don't look away!'
interaction: TV: the dark world (cave, shipwreck, haunted attic), one beam per phone, a found-object tally and a 30 s round timer. Phone: screen black, held like a torch; orientation = beam direction, tap = recalibrate by pointing at the TV centre, long press = narrow bright beam. Remote: OK starts a round or re-centres everyone (keeps Vega awake), Back returns to the lobby.
mechanism: Phone: DeviceOrientationEvent yaw/pitch relative to a calibration pose, sent at ~30 Hz over couch-link (player name = beam colour). TV: a full-screen dark overlay made of stacked Views and a radial-alpha PNG 'beam' Image placed by Animated transforms (no SVG); creatures are Image sprites with one rule: advance only while outside every beam, freeze inside one. Optional: the coach-agent template (Strands on Bedrock AgentCore) narrates each round from the event log ('the thing reached the sofa twice'), rule-based fallback otherwise.
demo_honesty: One adult alone in a dim room: pair, calibrate, sweep, find two objects, get caught once. Beam jitter and any recalibration stay in the cut. Claim 'the beam goes where you point after a one-tap calibration', not 'tracks the phone in 3D'.
biggest_risk: Yaw drift on Android (alpha comes from the magnetometer) makes the beam wander after a minute; mitigate with relative calibration, slow drift compensation and re-centre on tap. Must also stay un-scary enough for a family-entertainment pitch.

name: Statues
one_liner: Phones in pockets, the TV is 'it': play Red Light Green Light or Freeze Dance and the TV catches whoever moved.
impossible_on_phone: Every phone is in a pocket as a body sensor with no screen to look at; the 'it' who turns round has to be a face at the far end of the room that all the players watch at once.
ten_second_shot: A big cartoon face on the TV has its back turned; three people creep across the carpet. It spins round. Everyone freezes except one knee that wobbles. 'ANIL MOVED' flashes up with the wobble drawn as a jagged line. Groans.
interaction: TV: the 'it' character (back turned / facing you), the carpet lane with each player's progress, callouts by name, a Freeze Dance mode with music stops. Phone: in a pocket, motion only; buzzes briefly when caught. Remote: OK starts a round (keeps Vega awake), Left/Right picks the mode, Back ends.
mechanism: Phone: DeviceMotionEvent acceleration magnitude at 60 Hz, reduced on the phone to a 100 ms 'stillness score' (variance over a window against a baseline taken during a 2 s 'stand still' at round start) streamed over couch-link; the relay clock (serverNow) lets the TV judge 'moved after the turn' fairly across phones with different latency. TV: round state machine; the 'it' turns at random intervals and learns to fake a turn. Freeze Dance music comes from the laptop or from the phones' speakers in sync via serverNow (TV audio on the simulator is unreliable). Optional: the coach-agent shape (Strands on Bedrock AgentCore) writes the 'it' character's taunt from the round log; canned lines as fallback.
demo_honesty: One adult can demo it: phone in pocket, creep, freeze, get caught on purpose once; a friend turns it into a race. Thresholds are shown as they are; the video claims it catches 'a step or a wobble', not small movements.
biggest_risk: Sensitivity fairness: a loose pocket or a cheap sensor gives false 'moved' calls. Mitigate with a per-phone baseline, a visible 'how still is still' meter during calibration, and the jagged replay line so a disputed call is explainable.
crowding_keywords: motion sensor party game phone pocket

name: Porthole
one_liner: The TV becomes a window: a phone under it sees where you stand, the view shifts as you walk, creatures react as you approach.
impossible_on_phone: A window only works when the surface is large, fixed in the room and you are the one moving; a handheld screen moves with you, so it can only ever be a lens, never a window.
ten_second_shot: A kid walks from the left of the sofa to the right; through the porthole the reef slides and a whale's eye that was hidden behind the frame edge comes into view. The kid steps towards the TV and the clownfish dart into the anemone. Steps back; they creep out again.
interaction: TV: the window scene (reef, spaceship porthole, castle courtyard) with layered parallax and creatures that hide or approach depending on your distance and angle. Phone: propped under the TV, front camera facing the sofa, runs face detection locally and sends only (x, y, size) of the nearest face; its screen is black. Remote: OK switches scene (keeps Vega awake), Up/Down sets parallax strength, Back pauses.
mechanism: Phone browser: getUserMedia front camera plus an in-browser face detector (Chrome's FaceDetector where present, otherwise MediaPipe Face Detection from a CDN, ~10-15 fps at 480p); only the nearest face's normalised x, y and box size leave the phone at ~10 Hz over couch-link, never video. TV: 3-5 Image layers wider than the screen translated by Animated transforms at rates proportional to depth, a one-euro-style smoothing filter on the TV to kill jitter, and creature behaviours keyed off face size (distance) and x (angle). Optional: the coach-agent shape (Strands on Bedrock AgentCore) gives the creatures short lines when a child lingers.
demo_honesty: One adult: prop the phone, walk slowly across the room, lean in and step back; split-screen the sofa and the TV so the judge sees the walk and the shift together. State 'nearest face, about 3 m, normal room light'; do not claim multi-viewer or 3D.
biggest_risk: Latency plus jitter makes the parallax sloppy or nauseating, and the phone camera's range in a dim living room. Mitigate with smoothing, modest parallax, and a 'creatures react' mode that still works at 2-3 Hz.

name: Stick Charades
one_liner: Charades where the TV is your teammate: a propped phone turns you into a stick figure and the TV blurts guesses live for the room.
impossible_on_phone: The performer acts two or three metres from the camera, hands free and facing the room, and the guesses must be readable by everyone including the performer; a phone can be the eye or the scoreboard, not both.
ten_second_shot: A giant stick figure on the TV mirrors the dad flapping his arms. Guesses pop up underneath and get crossed out: 'Bird? ... Juggling? ... Chicken!' The family yells 'NO' as he starts to swim. The TV: 'Swimming. Final answer.' Cheer.
interaction: TV: the stage: a live stick figure, a timer, the stream of guesses with confidence, and a running score of 'TV got it' vs 'TV failed'. Phone: propped on a table pointed at the performer, runs pose landmarks locally, screen black; an optional second phone is the private card that shows the secret word to the performer. Remote: OK starts a round (keeps Vega awake), Right skips, Back ends.
mechanism: Phone: MediaPipe Pose (CDN, in-browser) at ~15 fps -> 17 landmarks at ~10 Hz over couch-link for the live stick figure; every 2-3 s the phone rasterises a 4-frame stick-figure strip on a canvas (~256 px, a few KB), so only a skeleton ever leaves the phone. TV: draws the figure with twelve rotated Views (no SVG). Guessing: the coach-agent shape (Strands on Bedrock AgentCore) with a vision-capable Bedrock model receives the strip plus the round's eight candidate words (or none in hard mode) and returns a guess, a confidence and a one-line reason; the TV shows successive guesses; the rule-based fallback is 'pass'.
demo_honesty: One adult: prop the phone, act 'swimming', 'climbing', 'sleeping' and one it gets wrong, and keep the wrong one in the video. Report the measured hit rate on a 20-word set in the README instead of saying 'the TV understands you'. Say 'only stick figures leave the phone'.
biggest_risk: Guess accuracy from stick-figure strips and the 5-8 s Bedrock round trip. Mitigate with the candidate list, streaming partial guesses and a hard-mode disclaimer; if Bedrock quota is zero the game still runs as a stick-figure mirror with the family guessing.
